pr_body:
If you pass an Artifact or FilesToRunProvider to
Builder.setExecutable, it will now use the
callable path, not just the execpath.

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/13189

Unfortunately, call sites that pass PathFragment
are susceptible to the bug, because PathFragment
is inherently ambiguous: if it's a bare file name,
the shell resolves it against PATH, otherwise
against the current directory.

RELNOTES: none

issue_context.title: Starlark: ctx.actions.run creates wrong argv0 when executable is top-level tool
issue_context.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

`ctx.actions.run(executable = x, ...)` won't work when `x` is a label in the root package (e.g. `//:bin.sh`).

The spawn will have `x` as argv0 (resolved against the PATH) instead of `./x`.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

<details>

<summary>Sources (click to expand):</summary>

`//:BUILD`:

```starlark
load("foo.bzl", "foo")

foo(
    name = "x",
    out = "x.out",
    tool = "bin.sh",
)

genrule(
    name = "y",
    outs = ["y.out"],
    cmd = "$(location bin.sh) $@",
    tools = ["bin.sh"],
)
```

`//:foo.bzl`:

```starlark
def _impl(ctx):
    ctx.actions.run(
        outputs = [ctx.outputs.out],
        executable = ctx.executable.tool,
        arguments = [ctx.outputs.out.path],
    )
    return [DefaultInfo(files = depset([ctx.outputs.out]))]

foo = rule(
    implementation = _impl,
    attrs = {
        "tool": attr.label(allow_single_file = True, executable = True, cfg = "host"),
        "out": attr.output(mandatory = True),
    },
)
```

`//:bin.sh`:
```sh
#!/bin/bash
echo hello $0 > $1
```

</details>

Building the Starlark rule fails, because `bin.sh` is not on the PATH (should be `./bin.sh`):

```
  $ bazel --ignore_all_rc_files build -s //:x
Starting local Bazel server and connecting to it...
INFO: Analyzed target //:x (4 packages loaded, 7 targets configured).
INFO: Found 1 target...
SUBCOMMAND: # //:x [action 'Action x.out', configuration: 86d23d2b5aedbeecfc6e6954ea9486ec39e9e40bcbc4b17cec46a06eed198d11, execution platform: @local_config_platform//:host]
(cd /home/laszlo/.cache/bazel/_bazel_laszlo/bc5487f033a0af65dff1ff0bd4000d75/execroot/__main__ && \
  exec env - \
  bin.sh bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/x.out)
ERROR: /tmp/foo/BUILD:3:4: Action x.out failed: (Exit 1): bin.sh failed: error executing command bin.sh bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/x.out

Use --sandbox_debug to see verbose messages from the sandbox bin.sh failed: error executing command bin.sh bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/x.out

Use --sandbox_debug to see verbose messages from the sandbox
src/main/tools/linux-sandbox-pid1.cc:390: "execvp(bin.sh, 0x1d97d60)": No such file or directory
Target //:x failed to build
Use --verbose_failures to see the command lines of failed build steps.
INFO: Elapsed time: 1.748s, Critical Path: 0.06s
INFO: 2 processes: 2 internal.
FAILED: Build did NOT complete successfully
```

But building the essentially same genrule works because argv0 is `/bin/bash`:

```
  $ bazel --ignore_all_rc_files build -s //:y
INFO: Analyzed target //:y (1 packages loaded, 2 targets configured).
INFO: Found 1 target...
SUBCOMMAND: # //:y [action 'Executing genrule //:y', configuration: 86d23d2b5aedbeecfc6e6954ea9486ec39e9e40bcbc4b17cec46a06eed198d11, execution platform: @local_config_platform//:host]
(cd /home/laszlo/.cache/bazel/_bazel_laszlo/bc5487f033a0af65dff1ff0bd4000d75/execroot/__main__ && \
  exec env - \
    PATH=/home/laszlo/app:/home/laszlo/app:/home/laszlo/google-cloud-sdk/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/games:/usr/local/games:/snap/bin:/home/laszlo/app/google-cloud-sdk/bin:/home/laszlo/app/google-cloud-sdk/bin \
  /bin/bash -c 'source external/bazel_tools/tools/genrule/genrule-setup.sh; ./bin.sh bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/y.out')
Target //:y up-to-date:
  bazel-bin/y.out
INFO: Elapsed time: 0.146s, Critical Path: 0.05s
INFO: 2 processes: 1 internal, 1 linux-sandbox.
INFO: Build completed successfully, 2 total actions
```

I have a copy of `//:bin.sh` under `//:tool/bin.sh`. After changing the `foo` rule's `tool` arg to that, the build works:

```
  $ bazel --ignore_all_rc_files build -s //:x
INFO: Analyzed target //:x (1 packages loaded, 2 targets configured).
INFO: Found 1 target...
SUBCOMMAND: # //:x [action 'Action x.out', configuration: 86d23d2b5aedbeecfc6e6954ea9486ec39e9e40bcbc4b17cec46a06eed198d11, execution platform: @local_config_platform//:host]
(cd /home/laszlo/.cache/bazel/_bazel_laszlo/bc5487f033a0af65dff1ff0bd4000d75/execroot/__main__ && \
  exec env - \
  tool/bin.sh bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/x.out)
Target //:x up-to-date:
  bazel-bin/x.out
INFO: Elapsed time: 0.122s, Critical Path: 0.04s
INFO: 2 processes: 1 internal, 1 linux-sandbox.
INFO: Build completed successfully, 2 total actions
```

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Ubuntu 20.04

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

```
release 4.0.0
```

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

Looked at the open issues with "top-level" in them, but didn't find a relevant one.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?
comments:
One more nuance is about `ctx.actions.run`: `executable` can take a File, or a string, or a FilesToRunProvider.

If it's a string, then we should leave it as-is, and let it be resolved against the PATH. But if it's a File or FilesToRunProvider, then it should get a `./` prefix.
